questions.question: Why can't the engine just add up the five first-order formulas to explain a week's change in n?
options: The formulas need data that the filings don't give
The causes interact: a price move changes n, which changes the m and q each later action lands at, so first-order values don't sum to the observed change
First-order formulas only work for Strategy
The formulas are in dollars and n is in coins
questions.explanation: First-order values treat each action alone. The engine applies the parts one at a time and recomputes n exactly after each, so they sum to the observed change.

questions.question: What is "value to common" on the page?
options: The dollars a firm raised in a week
The market value of the common stock
Δn × S × p, a change in net coins per share converted to dollars at the week's S and p
The dividend paid to common shareholders
questions.explanation: The ruler is coins per share; multiplying by S and p turns it into dollars for all shares at the week's coin price.

questions.question: In what order does `attribute()` split a week?
options: Actions, price, carry, residual
Price, itm_flip, each action in actions.csv order, carry, est_issuance (BitMine), residual
itm_flip, price, carry, actions, residual
Residual first, then each action by size
questions.explanation: The fixed order is decision A1: price, in-the-money flips, actions at their own prices, carry, BitMine's estimated issuance, and the residual last.

questions.question: Strategy's week ending 2026-09-20 has parts price +$711.7M, itm_flip +$125.3M, buy_coin +$1.1M, retire_pref +$3.1M, carry −$57.4M and residual −$2.9M. What is the observed change in value to common?
questions.explanation: The identity says the rows including the residual sum to the observed change: 711.7 + 125.3 + 1.1 + 3.1 − 57.4 − 2.9 = 780.9.

questions.question: BitMine issued $350.0M of BMNP notional at $80 (q = 0.80) and received $273.8M net. Why does `dn_exact` sit below `dn_first_order`?
options: Exact books the $350.0M of notional issued for $273.8M; first order treats the $273.8M as sold at q = 0.80 ($342.25M), so the gap is the $6.2M of fees divided by q, $7.75M
The coin price moved during the week
First order ignores preferred stock
Exact values are always larger in magnitude by 10%
questions.explanation: Gross at $80 is $280.0M, net $273.8M, so fees are $6.2M. First order implies $342.25M of notional; exact books $350.0M, a $7.75M difference (6.2 / 0.80).
